scope: Independent review of the recorded RCW 9.96.060(2)/(6) applicability handoff for wa_vac_substance_use_disorder. The sole question is whether the subsection (2)(a)-(i) bar sentence governs the standalone subsection (6) treatment route.

question.text: Do the RCW 9.96.060(2)(a)-(i) bars govern a qualifying standalone RCW 9.96.060(6) substance use disorder treatment route?
question.answerScope: The subsection (2)(a)-(i) bar sentence does not govern the subsection (6) route because the current statute expressly excepts subsection (6). This answer does not decide any separate route, participant, filing, source, packet, review, or production condition.

primaryAuthorityVerification.title: RCW 9.96.060, Vacating records of conviction for misdemeanor and gross misdemeanor offenses
directReadLocations: current page lines 135-151 (subsection (2) opening and paragraphs (a)-(i))

observations.subsection2Opening: The current subsection (2) bar sentence begins with an express exception for subsections (3), (4), (5), and (6).
subsection2Bars: (a) incomplete sentence terms, including financial obligations
(b) pending criminal charges in state, other state, federal, or tribal court
(d) specified DUI, physical-control, railroad-intoxication, and prior-offense conditions
(h) new crime in the prior three years
(i) current or recent qualifying protection, no-contact, antiharassment, or civil-restraint order
observations.subsection6: The current subsection (6) separately covers enumerated drug convictions and provides a program-completion/proof path or qualifying assessment path with six months of substantial compliance and recovery progress reflected in a written status update; upon verification, the court must vacate the conviction or convictions.

primaryAuthorityVerification.relevance: The express subsection (6) exception is dispositive for the narrow applicability question; the separate text supplies the conditions that remain applicable.

primaryAuthorityVerification.title: 2023 sp.s. c. 1, § 11 (2E2SSB 5536), amendment to RCW 9.96.060
directReadLocations: PDF pages 15-17 lines 588-668 (section 11 amendment and subsection (2) exception/bar text)

observations.section11Subsection2: The enacted redline adds (6) to the parenthetical exceptions in subsection (2), alongside (3), (4), and (5).
observations.section11Subsection6: The same section adds the standalone subsection (6) treatment route, including the enumerated convictions, alternative proof paths, six-month compliance/progress condition, written status update, and mandatory vacatur upon verification.
observations.effectiveDate: Section 11 is among the sections stated to take effect July 1, 2023.

primaryAuthorityVerification.relevance: The enactment confirms that the subsection (6) exception and the separate treatment route were adopted together; it corroborates the current codified text.

determination.supportedInterpretation: For a qualifying RCW 9.96.060(6) applicant, the exclusion/bar list in RCW 9.96.060(2)(a)-(i) is outside the subsection (6) route. A subsection (2)(a)-(i) condition cannot by itself defeat that route; the applicant must still satisfy subsection (6) and all separately applicable requirements.
reasoning: The current RCW text uses an express exception before listing the subsection (2)(a)-(i) bars and names subsection (6).

Subsection (6) then states its own route-specific conviction, treatment/assessment, compliance/progress, written-status-update, proof, and verification conditions without incorporating the subsection (2)(a)-(i) list.
The 2023 session-law redline independently shows the insertion of (6) into the subsection (2) exception and the enactment of subsection (6) in the same amendment.
determination.confidenceBasis: Direct read of the current official RCW page and the enacted official 2023 session-law amendment; no secondary authority was needed for this bounded question.
